title: At the door of the Reform — what Verne got right
learning_goal: Know the Reform Club is real, founded 1836, Barry's palazzo of 1841, Soyer's kitchens, and Fogg's breakfast; feel cosy club warmth.

narration.script: We arrive at the door of Fogg's club. The Reform Club is real, and still here: 104 Pall Mall, since 1836. Its founders backed the great Reform Act of 1832 — hence the name. In the novel this is Fogg's whole world: he eats here, reads here, plays cards here, every day until midnight. Charles Barry's palazzo opened in 1841: Portland stone outside; inside, a saloon two storeys high under a glass roof. And the famous kitchens that the chef Alexis Soyer helped to plan. Look up — the tall windows of the first floor. Now Fogg's breakfast, taken here. A broiled fish with Reading sauce — keep that in mind. Roast beef, a tart, Cheshire cheese, and the tea the Reform is famous for. The front today; Barry's elevation. And here, the saloon engraved in 1841 — no camera has been inside for us. Somewhere in there, breakfast done, Fogg cuts the pages himself and reads The Times.

variants.clear: This is the door of Fogg's club: the Reform Club. It is real, and still here — 104 Pall Mall, since 1836. Its founders had backed the Reform Act of 1832 — that is where the name comes from. In the book, Fogg spends every day here until midnight: meals, newspapers, cards. The architect Charles Barry finished the building in 1841. Stone outside; inside, a grand hall two floors high, under a glass roof. The club also had famous kitchens, planned with the chef Alexis Soyer. Look up at the tall windows. Here Fogg ate his breakfast: grilled fish with Reading sauce — remember that sauce. Roast beef, a fruit tart, cheese, and the club's famous tea. Now three pictures: the front today, the architect's plan of the front, and the great hall, drawn in 1841. No camera has been inside for us. Somewhere in there, Fogg cuts his newspaper's pages and reads The Times.

production_notes: No footage of the interior exists (manifest search note) — never fake it. Order (QA): arrival + history over the video 0–25 s; the 'look up' cue and the breakfast over the video's last 20 s (25–45 s, we are 'at the door') with the menu on the caption at 30–42 s so the guide reads only the best clause; the photo trio lines over M-20 + insets 45–70 s. The 'look up' cue does NOT name the coffee-room: its nine windows are in the long SOUTH (garden) wall (F-15), not on the Pall Mall front — Narrator, keep it that way, and keep 'nine' out of this scene (Quiz A follows). No paper-knife: Towle says he cuts the uncut Times 'with a skill which betrayed familiarity' (F-06). Narrator: ≤ 140 words, every sentence ≤ 20 words (Continuity #2); ends on the noun. Linear cut (A5, clear track): 62 s cap, from the door — M-20 for 38 s, then the M-22 / M-23 insets (M-01 is used by 04 count-the-steps, player only). Keep s:0 and s:2: without them the film opened on 'It is real, and still here…' with no antecedent and never said where the club's name comes from. The Soyer kitchens and the closing Times line pay for those seconds. A8 2026-08-19 (content-preparer): M-01 marked `use: player`; M-69c added as a second façade angle for the linear cut. This beat was never a walking shot, so it never needed a clip card — rights-a6.md §3.6 'YES, and the slow push is now allowed on the BY-SA stills'.
